objective: Choose the smallest reliable durable-execution spine before domain migrations.

candidate-dbos.reason: Corrected Hatchet admission restored the three-challenger cap; reserve did not need the destructive bake-off.

selection_basis: The incumbent fails mandatory same-run recovery/resume/cancel/retry/move/replay semantics and cannot remain the durable-execution winner.
Restate, Temporal and Hatchet all passed the frozen semantic hard gate with no duplicate simulated external effects.
The Phase 3A objective is the smallest reliable spine, not the most feature-rich platform.

Restate combines full semantic PASS with the simplest basic self-host shape, no external database requirement for the basic deployment, the lowest recorded wall time in this fixture, and dedicated snapshot/backup plus upgrade/rollback operational surfaces.

Temporal is retained as fallback because it provides the strongest mature history/inspection and self-host operations story, but its production topology and sequential schema/server upgrade discipline are heavier.

Hatchet passes semantics but loses on operational footprint for this use case: PostgreSQL is required in the tested shape, recovery/reassignment was slower, and operator replay re-executed internal tasks even though effect-level idempotency prevented duplicate external effects.
Unknown/null Restate and Temporal CPU/RAM/network fields were not converted to zero and were not used as a hidden advantage.
promotion_limits: This verdict selects a Phase 3A runtime winner only; it does not install a new production writer or transfer production authority.

Before production use, the Integration Factory must configure identity/policy, credentials, observability, health probes, backup/restore drill, regression tests, rollback, service/autostart management and SHADOW/PILOT gates.
Existing production work retains priority until a later explicit production promotion receipt.
